scope_note: Identification, deduplication, and journal-filtering ran at full-corpus scale (1316 -> 871 -> 368 records). From title/abstract screening onward, no full-corpus production funnel was executed; instead each downstream stage's classifier/extractor/synthesizer was validated against Thabit et al. 2025's own published gold data (Appendix A/B, Table C1) on a deliberately cost-bounded sample. The PRISMA-style fields above therefore stop at journal-filter by design -- see validation_summary below, NOTES.md, and manuscript S13 for what was actually measured at each downstream stage and why this is presented as a documented scope limitation, not a claim of full reproduction.

title_abstract_screening.method: mini model screens all known records first; only its exclude/borderline decisions escalate to a flagship model for a second look (recall-first cascade, screening_cascade.py), same checklist prompt both passes

full_text_eligibility.method: FT_SCREENING module pilot run on 20 records (10 known_included + 10 known_excluded); all initial processing failures recovered on retry, 20/20 completed

deductive_extraction.method: single-LLM-pass deductive coding against a 37-concept codebook, scored per-publication and micro-averaged against Table C1 gold, 10 known_included pilot full texts, 4 prompt variants plus a zero-cost post-hoc cutoff sweep
deductive_extraction.best_f1: v4, top-K=28-by-strength cutoff: P=0.465 R=0.842 F1=0.600
deductive_extraction.baseline_f1_range: 0.567-0.600 across all variants and sweep points -- a real ceiling, not an undertuned prompt (see NOTES.md)

theme_synthesis.method: one LLM call per theme (6 themes total), aggregative cross-study synthesis prose built only from the deductive extraction's v2 found/quote evidence, 10 known_included pilot articles
theme_synthesis.comparison: qualitatively compared against Thabit et al.'s own Findings-section prose theme by theme; structural coverage tracks closely, no qualitative failures (no hallucinated pattern, wrong direction, or fabricated quote); two systematic, expected differences present in every theme (smaller evidence pool, citation by article title not author-year key)
